name: RAMESH KRISHNAN
bio:
Career Overview: Playing Style: A crafty baseliner with exceptional touch, finesse, and a single-handed backhand, excelling on clay and grass courts.
Career-High ATP Singles Ranking: #23 (January 28, 1985).
Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the quarterfinals of Wimbledon (1986), US Open (1981, 1987), and Australian Open (1987).
Notable Achievements: ATP Titles: Won 7 singles titles, including back-to-back victories in 1986 (Tokyo Outdoor, Metz). Davis Cup & National Representation: Instrumental in India’s 1987 Davis Cup final run, defeating top players like John McEnroe and Wally Masur, with a career Davis Cup record of 29-18.
Other Highlights: Son of Ramanathan Krishnan, a pre-Open Era legend. Won the Wimbledon and French Open junior titles in 1979. Known for his tactical brilliance and understated style.
Ramesh retired in 1993, remembered as one of India’s finest singles players of the Open Era. 🎾🇮🇳
